selected_original.title: Microsoft Visual Basic 1.0 for Windows - Edit
selected_original.depicts: Microsoft Visual Basic [design] IDE on a Windows 3.x desktop: menu bar, properties bar (property list 'Caption' = '7', position 120, 600, size 495 x 495), 16-cell toolbox, 'Calculator' form in the form designer with the '7' button selected, CALC.MAK project window (Global.bas, CALC.FRM), and the CALC.FRM code window showing Sub Number_Click (Index As Integer).

creator.software_and_ui: Microsoft Corporation (the companion About capture shows 'Copyright (c) 1987-1991 Microsoft Corp.' and 'Portions of this product were developed for Microsoft by Cooper Software, Inc.')
creator.screenshot_capture: unknown - uncredited WinWorld contributor; no name on the file, screenshot page or product page

selected_original.original_publication_date: 1991 (software release year stated by WinWorld; not a capture date)
selected_original.earliest_confirmed_public_date: 2026-07-08 (Wayback Machine capture 20260708105836 of the WinWorld product page, which references this file name)
selected_original.depicted_event_date: unknown - an undated session of Visual Basic 1.0; not a 1991 photograph
selected_original.access_method: Anonymous HTTPS GET (curl 8.21.0) of the public image URL; no account, terms acceptance, CAPTCHA or download gate. The Wayback copy of the image could not be fetched (web.archive.org refused connections from this machine after the page capture was read), so the live WinWorld file was used.

file_integrity.note: The MD5 equals the hash embedded in WinWorld's own file name, so the acquired bytes are the file WinWorld stores.

version_evidence: WinWorld labels the file 'Microsoft Visual Basic 1.0 for Windows - Edit' and shows it on its Microsoft Visual Basic 1.0 product page (release date 1991) - host attribution, not in-frame proof.

Companion capture evidence/version-evidence/about-original.png, shown beside it in the same WinWorld carousel, displays 'About Microsoft Visual Basic' with 'Microsoft Visual Basic Version 1.0' and 'Copyright (c) 1987-1991 Microsoft Corp.' over the same IDE.

The two captures match in resolution (640x480, 4-bit), title-bar text 'Microsoft Visual Basic [design]', menu (File Edit Code Run Window Help), properties-bar layout, 16-cell toolbox icons and the minimised File Manager / Program Manager desktop icons at the same positions - consistent with one installation. This is visual correlation, not proof that the Edit capture was taken in the same session.
